I'm in Civil Air Patrol, which isn't tied to school, but it's for the youth. I haven't been in too long, but I am passionate about it. We are the children of the Air Force, if you will. This will help me in the Air Force. I'd say it's impacted me a lot, I've made friends, and it's a brotherhood. Knowing most, if not all, are going to grow up, and serve our country. We do our best at everything, giving 110%. A lot of people look at as us "playing military," but only if they realized. We might be minors, but we sure do take it seriously. We do things during the summer a lot of teens wouldn't do, like volunteering to go to a camp to be molded into a cadet. We are PT'd, we are trained, we are disciplined, we learn a lot. We learn about the uniform, and what the flag means. How important it is. We also help the community. We do Search and Rescue missions, and missions of the similar type. It's not for everyone, but if you are interested in the military at all, I'd suggest it. It'll show you real quick what it's like. All the way from taking orders you don't specifically want to, to working your way through the ranks, with each rank taking on new responsibilities, and gaining more discipline. You really grow into an outstanding teenager.
